title: Molecular locking of lithium ions for improved efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells - Nature Energy
gist: Nanjing Tech University paper (abstract-only preview) introduces phosphonate-based molecules with cyano chains (DCEP) that 'lock' lithium ions in the Spiro-OMeTAD hole-transport layer, curbing Li+ migration and tBP loss; n–i–p perovskite cells reach 26.73% efficiency and retain 91–95% after 1,000–1,600 h of light, 85 °C and bias stress tests.

insights.claim: The widely used perovskite hole-transport material Spiro-OMeTAD suffers instabilities from hygroscopicity and lithium-ion migration caused by its LiTFSI and 4-tert-butylpyridine (tBP) dopant additives.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Dopant-driven degradation in the hole-transport layer is a core bankability barrier for n–i–p perovskites; fixes here target a key failure mode for commercialization.

insights.claim: Phosphonate-based molecules with extended cyano chains coordinate lithium ions at two sites, regulating Li+ mobility and stabilizing the LiTFSI/tBP dopant environment in Spiro-OMeTAD hole-transport layers.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: A drop-in additive approach that keeps Spiro-OMeTAD rather than replacing it could be easier to adopt in existing perovskite process lines.
insights.quote: enabling dual-site coordination with lithium ions to regulate ion mobility

insights.claim: The phosphonate additive also reduces tBP loss, strengthens the thermomechanical robustness of the Spiro-OMeTAD matrix, mitigates dopant redistribution and stabilizes the interface, with these coupled effects improving stability under illumination, heat and electrical bias.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Multi-stress improvement (light, heat, bias) matters more to module qualification than single-test gains.

insights.claim: Supplementary videos show a DCEP-modified Spiro device with substantially improved resistance to water-induced degradation compared with a control Spiro device whose underlying perovskite layer degraded rapidly under deionized water exposure.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Moisture resistance addresses the hygroscopicity weakness and could reduce encapsulation demands, a cost lever for perovskite modules.
insights.quote: showing substantially improved resistance to water-induced degradation

insights.claim: Optimized n–i–p perovskite solar cells using the lithium-locking phosphonate additive reached a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.73%.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: 26.73% is in the top tier for single-junction perovskites; the claim pairs record-class efficiency with stability, the combination investors need to see.

insights.claim: The lithium-locked perovskite cells retained 95% of initial efficiency after 1,000 h of maximum power point tracking (ISOS-L-1), 95% after 1,000 h at 85 °C (ISOS-L-2) and 91% after 1,600 h under 1.5 V bias (ISOS-V-1).
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Lab-scale protocol results are encouraging but still far from 25-year field life; watch for module-scale and IEC-certification data before treating as commercial de-risking.
insights.quote: retain 95% of the initial efficiency after 1,000 h under maximum power point tracking

insights.claim: The lithium-locking perovskite work comes from Nanjing Tech University's State Key Laboratory of Flexible Electronics led by Yonghua Chen, Lingfeng Chao and Wei Huang, funded by the Natural Science Foundation of China, the National Key R&D Program of China and Jiangsu provincial programs.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Continued state-funded Chinese leadership in perovskite stability research reinforces China's position to commercialize next-generation PV first.
